content.value_statement: Complex threats are difficult to compare when attack paths and dependencies remain implicit. This skill structures paths, scores leaf nodes, maps mitigations, and highlights defense priorities.
actual_capabilities: Defines attacker goals and decomposes them into AND and OR branches.
Annotates leaf attacks with difficulty, cost, time, detection risk, and mitigations.
Identifies easiest, cheapest, and lowest-detection paths from supplied tree data.
Analyzes mitigation coverage and highlights nodes shared across multiple paths.
Provides reference patterns for Mermaid, PlantUML, and structured data exports.
Prioritizes mitigations by their estimated impact across modeled paths.
limitations: Does not validate assumptions against a live environment or execute security tests.
Scores depend on analyst judgment and are not calibrated with empirical threat data.
Provides reference snippets, not a tested application or executable package.
Can expose sensitive attack paths if outputs are shared beyond authorized stakeholders.

use_cases.title: Design Security Controls
use_cases.description: Map likely paths to a protected asset and identify controls that interrupt the most branches.

use_cases.title: Scope Authorized Assessments
use_cases.description: Turn an approved attacker objective into explicit test paths, assumptions, and defensive validation targets.

use_cases.title: Explain Risk Priorities
use_cases.description: Present threat dependencies and mitigation coverage in a structure that supports investment decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Tree
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an attack tree for [system]. Use [authorized attacker goal] as the root. Separate AND and OR nodes. Add one mitigation per leaf.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner modeling for a clearly scoped asset

prompt_templates.title: Add Path Attributes
prompt_templates.prompt: Expand this attack tree: [tree]. Rate each leaf by cost, skill, time, and detection risk. State assumptions and suggest defensive controls.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Mitigation Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [tree] and [existing controls]. Identify open paths, shared critical nodes, and controls with the greatest estimated coverage. Keep attack details non-operational.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Defensive Scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the current and proposed controls for [authorized scope]. Recalculate path exposure, explain uncertainty, and produce separate technical and executive summaries.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced decision support across control options

output_examples.input: Model unauthorized access to a customer portal protected by passwords and multifactor authentication.
output: Root goal: Gain unauthorized portal access.
OR branch: Obtain valid credentials through approved threat scenarios.
AND branch: Acquire a session and bypass the additional verification control.
Priority controls: Phishing-resistant authentication, rate limits, session protection, and support verification.

output_examples.input: Prioritize controls for an attack tree with several paths sharing an exposed administrative interface.
output: Critical node: Reach the administrative interface.
Coverage finding: Restricting interface access interrupts the largest number of modeled paths.
Next controls: Strong administrator authentication, network restrictions, monitoring, and recovery procedures.

output_examples.input: Summarize an attack tree for an executive review.
output_examples.output: The model identifies three major threat paths and two shared control gaps. Access restrictions and stronger identity controls provide the broadest estimated risk reduction.

best_practices: Confirm authorization, scope, protected assets, and the attacker goal before building the tree.
Record assumptions and use consistent scales for difficulty, cost, time, and detection.
Attach mitigations to every leaf and review the model with relevant technical experts.
anti_patterns: Do not include operational exploit steps, malware instructions, or real credentials.
Do not treat subjective scores as measured probabilities or verified environment facts.
Do not publish sensitive attack paths outside the authorized stakeholder group.

faq.question: What inputs are required?
faq.answer: Provide the protected asset, authorized scope, attacker goal, known controls, assumptions, and the audience for the output.

faq.question: Does this skill execute attacks?
faq.answer: No. It produces models and reference templates without testing systems, running exploits, or collecting environment data.

faq.question: How are AND and OR nodes used?
faq.answer: An AND node requires every child condition. An OR node requires any one child path.

faq.question: Can it create diagram formats?
faq.answer: The playbook provides reference exporters for Mermaid and PlantUML representations of an attack tree.

faq.question: How reliable are the path scores?
faq.answer: Scores are comparative estimates based on supplied assumptions. Validate them with environment evidence and qualified reviewers.

faq.question: How should sensitive scenarios be handled?
faq.answer: Use only authorized scopes, keep details non-operational, include mitigations, and restrict distribution to approved stakeholders.
